items.title: Vn-Index closes at a fresh 2026 high on foreign buying
items.content: The index added 1.4% as foreign institutions turned net buyers for the eighth consecutive session, led by banks and steel.

items.title: State bank keeps refinancing rate unchanged for a third month
items.content: Policymakers held the rate steady, citing anchored inflation and a stable đồng, leaving room to act if exports soften.

items.title: Vinamilk posts a 12% rise in first-half dairy exports
items.content: The dairy giant shipped more than 900 million tonnes across Southeast Asia, aided by stronger demand from the Philippines.

items.title: Rubber prices ease as the rainy season eases supply
items.content: Natural rubber futures slipped 2% on the week as southern plantations resumed full tapping after weeks of heavy rain.

items.title: Dong holds steady against the dollar through July
items.content: The central bank's daily fixing stayed within a narrow band all month, a sign of calm in currency markets.

items.title: Bank lenders extend credit growth guidance for the half
items.content: Regulators signalled another 2 percentage points of room for lending growth, buoying the big four's share prices.

items.title: Steel exports to the EU climb as quotas wind down
items.content: Mills shipped 14% more tonnage in Q2, the last full quarter before softer quotas take effect next year.

items.title: Tech names lead HOSE turnover to a six-month high
items.content: Retail participation lifted daily turnover above VNĐ 22 trillion as investors rotated into software and chips.

items.title: Seafood sector shakes off red-tape delays
items.content: Export approvals normalised after a port backlog cleared, restoring shrimp shipments to pre-year pace.

items.title: Inflation prints 2.1%, within the state target band
items.content: The July reading stayed comfortably under the 4% ceiling, keeping rate expectations flat into the autumn.

items.title: Logistics stocks rally on new north-south rail tender
items.content: Shippers rose after the transport ministry opened the first package of the long-awaited corridor to bidding.

items.title: Coffee futures firm as arabica stocks tighten
items.content: Inventories at monitored warehouses fell for the fourth week, underpinning prices at harvest-adjacent levels.

items.title: Retail sales hold up despite the heat of the quarter
items.content: Monthly spending rose 0.9%, with e-commerce continuing to take share from physical shelves.

items.title: Private lenders rush to list structured deposits
items.content: Three mid-tier banks brought certificate products to market this month, chasing savers' renewed appetite.

items.title: Property developers stabilise as interest costs plateau
items.content: Major listed builders reported their first quarter without rising financing charges since 2023.

items.title: Rice export prices edge lower on regional harvest
items.content: Thai and Vietnamese cargoes eased in tandem as the summer crop reached buyers earlier than expected.

items.title: Manufacturing PMI slips but stays in expansion
items.content: The July reading eased to 50.4 as new export orders cooled, though employment and output both rose.

items.title: Green bonds debut on the local corporate market
items.content: The first certified green issuance priced at a 12-point discount to ordinary paper, drawing fund demand.

items.title: Airlines hedge fuel into the busy travel window
items.content: Carriers locked in jet fuel at July levels, shielding summer-fare margins from a firmer crude tape.

items.title: Cement volumes recover on resumed public works
items.content: Infrastructure spending re-accelerated after the rainy season, lifting domestic dispatches for a third month.

items.title: Pharma majors clear a vaccine re-registration hurdle
items.content: Two listed producers won renewed import licences, ending months of clearance uncertainty for their pipelines.

items.title: Savings rates tick up as banks compete for deposits
items.content: One-year deposit quotes inched 15 basis points higher at the top lenders, a modest nudge to the bond curve.

items.title: UPCOM listings double as SMEs test the public market
items.content: A dozen companies joined the unlisted board this quarter, more than in all of last year combined.

items.title: Garment orders shift back toward Vietnam
items.content: Buyers returned to the country's mills as a rival supplier's capacity tightened, lifting order books into Q4.
